LESSON: READING 3.4.1 POEMS: STRUCTURE

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we read or recite poems?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the structure of a poem
2. create a poem based on a topic of interest
3. appreciate the reading of poetry for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 3.4.1 POEMS: STRUCTURE
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 3.4.1 POEMS: STRUCTURE
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Describe the structure of a poem

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the structure of a poem. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the structure of a poem.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the structure of a poem. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a poem based on a topic of interest

What this means
In this part you learn to create a poem based on a topic of interest. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a poem based on a topic of interest.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a poem based on a topic of interest. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the reading of poetry for enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the reading of poetry for enjoyment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the reading of poetry for enjoyment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the reading of poetry for enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: describe the structure of a poem)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure to a partner. (skill: create a poem based on a topic of interest)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the reading of poetry for enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the structure of a poem.
3. Practise this skill: create a poem based on a topic of interest.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the reading of poetry for enjoyment.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we read or recite poems?
2. Why are non-living things or animals made to behave like human beings in poems or stories?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 3.4.1 Poems: Structure means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the structure of a poem.
5. Be able to: create a poem based on a topic of interest.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
